questions.explanation: Most candidates chose the correct turning effect. Many then chose D, believing the force on the left of the pivot equals the sum of the forces on the right. That leaves out the pivot. The pivot pushes up with force P, so the upward and downward forces balance: P = Q + R + S. For the turning effects, Q is a from the pivot on one side, R is a from it on the other side and S is 2a away: Q × a = R × a + S × 2a. Answer: B. In an equilibrium question, count the pivot's push as a force.

Most candidates recalled that ultrasound is used in medical scanning (statement 2). Many did not know that ultrasound diffracts less than audible sound (statement 1), so they chose D. Ultrasound has a higher frequency, so at the same speed its wavelength is shorter, and waves diffract less when the wavelength is small compared with the gap. Statement 3 is false: sound of any frequency travels at the same speed in air. Statements 1 and 2: A.

Many candidates chose C, 1.58, by using 44° as the angle of incidence. The 44° is measured between the ray and the surface of the block, not the normal, so the angle of incidence is 90 − 44 = 46°. The 26° is already measured from the normal. n = sin i / sin r = sin 46° / sin 26° = 0.719 / 0.438 = 1.64: D. Using 44° gives sin 44° / sin 26° = 1.58, which is option C. Draw the normal and check which angle sits against it.

Most candidates identified that a virtual image is formed. Many chose C, thinking the principal focus is where the image forms. P is where the dashed lines meet, which is the position of the virtual image. The principal focus is the point where a ray that leaves the object parallel to the axis crosses the axis after the lens. Follow the ray that runs horizontally from the top of the object: after the lens it crosses the axis at Q. So the focus is at Q: D.

Option D was the common wrong answer. The report says most candidates had the misconception that the kilowatt-hour is a unit of power transferred in one hour. It is a unit of energy, because energy = power × time: 1 kW for 1 hour. Power is already a rate, so power transferred in one hour is not a quantity at all. Answer: A.

The report found answers spread across all four options, suggesting many candidates guessed. It also noted that many worked out the force must be perpendicular to the field. That removes the two options along the field, A and C. Choosing between B and D needs the left-hand rule. The field runs from N to S, down the page. The electrons move into the page, so the conventional current points out of the page. First finger down, second finger out of the page, thumb to the right: B. Using the direction the electrons move as the current gives D.

Most candidates saw that this is a step-down transformer, so the secondary has 1200 × 12 / 240 = 60 turns. Many then chose B by working out the current in the lamp rather than in the mains wire. Lamp current: 36 / 12 = 3.0 A. A 100% efficient transformer has power in equal to power out, so the mains wire carries 36 / 240 = 0.15 A: A. Read the last line of the question to see which current it wants.

Many candidates identified nucleus X as helium-5 but did not notice the equation would not balance if Y were a beta particle. Check both totals. Left side: nucleon number 2 + 3 = 5 and charge 1 + 1 = 2. Helium-5 with a beta particle gives a charge of 2 + (−1) = 1, so that row fails. Helium-4 plus a neutron gives nucleon number 4 + 1 = 5 and charge 2 + 0 = 2, so both totals balance: C.

Many candidates did not allow for the background count. Option B, 2.4 min, is the time at which the total count rate has fallen to half its starting value (180 to 90 counts/min). Take the background off first. The source alone gives 180 − 20 = 160 counts/min at the start. Half of that is 80. The graph shows the total, so add the background back: 100 counts/min. The curve reaches 100 counts/min at 2.0 min: A. The report also notes that some removed the background at the start and then forgot to add it back after halving.

Most candidates used the correct rearrangement to find the orbital radius. Many then chose C by adding the radius of the Earth instead of subtracting it. A geostationary satellite has a period of 24 h = 86 400 s. r = vT / 2π = 3.1 × 86 400 / 2π = 4.26 × 10<sup>4</sup> km. That radius is measured from the centre of the Earth, and the question asks for the height above the surface: 42 600 − 6400 = 36 200 km, which is option A. Adding the radius gives 49 000 km, which is option C.
